title: Structs with More Fields
story: You landed a job at the school library! The librarian handed you a stack of new books and asked you to catalog them — title, author, and page count for each one.
why: Real-world data often has many fields. Structs grow naturally — just add more fields to capture everything you need.
analogy: A struct with more fields is like a longer form — more blanks to fill, but still one piece of paper that travels as a unit.
try_it: Add a `rating: Float64` field to the Book struct (1.0 to 5.0). Update all three books with ratings and print them alongside the title.
tips: Fields can be any type — mix Str, Int, Float64, and Bool in the same struct
Name fields clearly so you know what data they hold — `pages` is better than `num`
Group related data together — if multiple pieces describe the same thing, they belong in a struct
common_mistakes: Mixing up semicolons and commas — use semicolons in the type definition, commas when creating an instance
Creating all fields as Str when some should be Int or Float64 — use the type that matches the data
Forgetting to print some books after creating them — all instances should be verified
